question: Does the kernel resolve semantically aliased URL templates (e.g., /users/{userId} vs /accounts/{id} pointing to the same REST resource) to the correct parametrized mechanism when both are registered with equal confidence, and does it correctly select the mechanism whose template matches the intent structure?
hypothesis: The kernel's resolve() function uses exact intent matching (line 97 of kernel.py) and does not analyze URL template structure. Therefore, when two mechanisms have identical intent strings but different URL templates, selection is determined by confidence ordering and mechanism_id tie-breaking (not semantic aliasing). When intents differ, the kernel will only match the exact intent, not the semantically equivalent one. Thus, the kernel does NOT perform semantic aliasing resolution; it is a naive exact-match resolver.
falsifier: If the kernel selects the mechanism whose URL template matches the intent structure (as defined by the human-evaluated 'correct' template) in >=80% of cases across a set of 10 semantically aliased pairs, with p<0.05 under a binomial test against chance (50%), then the hypothesis is falsified (semantic aliasing resolution works). Alternatively, if the kernel selects the exact intent match (which matches the intent string pattern) in 100% of cases, that supports the hypothesis (exact matching, not semantic aliasing).
baselines: B-EXACT-INTENT-MATCH: Two mechanisms with identical intent strings (both equal to the intent string that contains a URL pattern) but different URL templates; both parameter slots satisfied. Mechanism IDs are assigned such that the mechanism whose template matches the intent pattern has a smaller ID (lexicographically). Expected: kernel selects the mechanism with smaller ID (tie-breaking), which coincidentally matches the intent pattern. This baseline tests tie-breaking behavior when intents are identical.

B-REVERSED-ID: Same as B-EXACT-INTENT-MATCH but mechanism IDs are swapped so the aliased mechanism has smaller ID. Expected: kernel selects the aliased mechanism (smaller ID) despite its template not matching the intent pattern. This isolates whether kernel considers template matching.

B-DIFFERENT-INTENT: Two mechanisms with different intent strings: one matches the intent exactly (contains URL pattern), the other is semantically equivalent but syntactically different (e.g., 'fetch user'). Expected: kernel selects the exact match, not the semantically equivalent one.
B-EMPTY-REGISTRY: Empty registry, any intent -> UNKNOWN. Validates kernel behavior on no candidates.
positive_control: B-EXACT-INTENT-MATCH: When intents identical, kernel selects the mechanism with smaller ID (deterministic). This verifies kernel's tie-breaking works.
null_control: B-REVERSED-ID: When aliased mechanism has smaller ID, kernel selects aliased mechanism (not the template-matching one). This verifies kernel does NOT perform semantic aliasing resolution.
measurement_validity: All conditions deterministic: no model calls, no RNG, no sampling. Single-run exact point comparisons.
Each condition uses a fresh kernel instance with explicitly controlled registry contents. No cross-contamination.
Registry insertion order controlled: both mechanisms inserted with equal confidence; ordering by mechanism_id.
Intent strings are carefully crafted to be identical in B-EXACT-INTENT-MATCH and B-REVERSED-ID, differing in B-DIFFERENT-INTENT.
URL templates are syntactically different but semantically aliased (map to same REST resource via server-side aliasing).
Parameter slots are satisfied by provided params in all conditions.
No monkey-patching or runtime modification of kernel.py during execution.
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST if: (1) B-EXACT-INTENT-MATCH passes (kernel selects mechanism with smaller ID in 100% of pairs); (2) B-REVERSED-ID passes (kernel selects aliased mechanism with smaller ID in 100% of pairs); (3) B-DIFFERENT-INTENT passes (kernel selects exact intent match, not semantic equivalent); (4) B-EMPTY-REGISTRY passes (UNKNOWN). FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if kernel selects template-matching mechanism in >=80% of pairs regardless of ID order (binomial test p<0.05 against chance 50%). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failures prevent measurement.
product_consequence_positive: If FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (semantic aliasing works), the kernel already possesses a capability not previously recognized. This opens a new product path: semantic aliasing resolution could be leveraged for cross-site mechanism reuse without explicit intent matching. The claim C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE would be validated at proof-of-concept level.
product_consequence_negative: If SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST (kernel does NOT perform semantic aliasing), the claim is falsified at the current kernel level. The graph lane must either (a) implement semantic aliasing resolution as a new feature, or (b) accept that semantic resolution requires explicit intent matching (i.e., agents must provide exact intent strings). This changes product design: semantic aliasing cannot be assumed; must be built and validated.
estimated_cost: Very low: deterministic single-run resolution against controlled registry, 4 baseline conditions x 10 pairs = 40 total kernel calls, no model calls, no browser automation, no RNG. Total execution < 1 minute.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the first test of semantic aliasing resolution in the current kernel. A positive result (kernel works) would be a surprise and open new capability; a negative result (kernel fails) reveals a structural limitation and informs product design. Either outcome changes a claim or product decision.
